examples.explain: "abb" has an extra b, so it is not an anagram of "ab".

hints: When are two words in the same group? Find something about a word that every anagram shares.
Sorting a word's letters gives the same string for all its anagrams. Use it as a dictionary key.
Even cheaper: a 26-slot letter count - turned into a tuple so it can be a key.

insight.oneLiner: Map every word to a key that all its anagrams share (sorted letters or letter counts), then bucket by key.

recall.a: Sorted letters, O(k log k); 26-count tuple, O(k).
recall.q: Name two canonical keys for an anagram class and their costs.

recall.a: Lists are mutable and unhashable; dict keys must be hashable.

insight.why: Grouping becomes a single dictionary pass: equal keys collide, and the hash map does the grouping for free.

oneLiner: Map every word to a key that all its anagrams share (sorted letters or letter counts), then bucket by key.

pitfalls.explain: Your key collides for words with different letter counts - e.g. a set of letters, or a sum of character codes.
pitfalls.title: Merged words that aren't anagrams

pitfalls.explain: Your key isn't canonical: two anagrams produced different keys.
pitfalls.title: Split anagrams into different groups

footnotes.text: Anagrams sort to the same string - sorting is a canonical form.

solutions.idea: Sort each word's letters to get a key shared by all its anagrams.
solutions.name: Key by sorted letters

footnotes.text: tuple(count), never the list itself - dict keys must be hashable. Counting is O(k) per word, cheaper than sorting's O(k log k).

solutions.idea: Count letters into 26 slots; the frozen counts are the key. No sorting needed.
solutions.name: Key by letter counts

starter:
class Solution:
    def groupAnagrams(self, strs: List[str]) -> List[List[str]]:
statement:
Given a list of strings `strs`, **group the words that are anagrams of each other** (same letters, same counts, any order).

Return the groups in any order; the words inside each group may also be in any order.
title: Group Anagrams
